cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is a prisoner on a ship headed for Italy (Acts 27:1), and a storm has been shoving that ship around for two weeks (Acts 27:14). It's the fourteenth night, they're still being driven across the Adriatic Sea, and the man writing this book is on board with them. Then, about midnight, the sailors start to sense something.

cards.question: About midnight on the fourteenth night, what do the sailors sense the ship is getting close to?

cards.text: So they drop a weighted line to check how deep the water is. Twenty fathoms. They go a little farther and check AGAIN.

cards.question: After a reading of twenty fathoms, the sailors go a little farther, and the next sounding reads ___ fathoms.

cards.text: Shallower water in the middle of the night, and they're scared of running aground on the rocks, so down go four anchors from the stern. It's that midnight walk across a dark kitchen when you KNOW you left a cookie sheet on the floor somewhere.

cards.question: With four anchors down from the stern, the sailors pray for daybreak.

cards.text: Meanwhile, the sailors get real busy up at the bow. They act like they're lowering more anchors from the front of the ship.

cards.question: Up at the bow, what are the sailors really letting down into the sea?

cards.text: Paul catches on that those sailors are trying to escape, and friend, two weeks in a storm as a PRISONER (Acts 27:1) and this man is STILL on top of it. He goes straight to the centurion, the Roman officer in charge of the prisoners (Acts 27:1), and the soldiers.

cards.question: What does Paul tell the centurion and the soldiers about the sailors lowering the lifeboat?

answers.text: If they leave you cannot be saved
Let them go so the ship is lighter
Lock them below deck until morning

cards.question: After Paul's warning, what do the soldiers do with the lifeboat?

answers.text: Cut the ropes and let it drift
Haul it back up on board
Tie it tight to the stern

cards.text: Right up to daybreak, Paul keeps working on everybody about one thing. After fourteen days of constant suspense, he tells them it's for their own preservation.

cards.question: Right up to daybreak, Paul keeps urging everyone on board to ___.
Paul tells the men that not a single hair of their heads will be lost.

cards.text: Fourteen days, and nobody's taken any food. Then Paul takes bread, gives thanks to God in front of them all, breaks it and starts eating.

cards.question: Watching Paul eat, the rest of the men on board stay too afraid to touch any food.

cards.text: They're all encouraged, and they take some food themselves. It's like when one person at work finally grabs a cookie from the break room box, and suddenly EVERYBODY'S lined up.
In all, there are 276 people on board, and friend, I get flustered when THREE people crowd around my oven. Once they've all eaten their fill, it's time to make the ship lighter.

cards.question: Once everyone on board has eaten their fill, how do they lighten the ship?

answers.text: Throw the grain into the sea

cards.text: When daylight finally comes, nobody recognizes the land. But they spot a bay with a sandy beach.

cards.question: When daylight comes, what do the people on the ship decide to do at the bay with the sandy beach?

cards.text: They cut away the anchors, loosen the ropes on the rudders and hoist the foresail to the wind. Here we go, friend, straight for the beach.

cards.question: The ship makes it all the way onto the sandy beach.

cards.text: The ship hits a sandbar and runs aground. The bow is stuck fast and won't move, and the stern is getting broken up by the waves, like a cookie glued to the pan on one end and crumbling on the other.

cards.question: With the ship breaking up, the soldiers plan to kill the prisoners so none of them can ___ to freedom.

cards.text: Those prisoners include Paul. But the centurion steps in and shuts the whole plan down.

cards.question: Why does the centurion stop the soldiers' plan to kill the prisoners?

answers.text: He wants to spare Paul's life
He needs every prisoner for trial
He is afraid of the sailors

cards.question: The centurion orders those who can swim to jump overboard first and get to land.

cards.text: That leaves everybody who can't swim, and friend, put me in THAT group. They're told to follow on something else.

cards.question: How are the people on the ship who can't swim told to get to land?

answers.text: On planks and parts of the ship

cards.question: Every one of the 276 people on board is brought safely to land.

cards.text: NOBODY looks cool floating to shore on a piece of a ship, but they ALL make it, friend. And trust me, this voyage isn't over yet.
